title: A sharp asymptotic spectral bound for forbidden subgraphs
abstract: For every fixed finite graph F of chromatic number r+1 at least three and every positive epsilon, there is an edge threshold M such that every finite simple F-free graph G with m at least M satisfies F2(A_G) <= 2(1-1/r)m - (2(1-1/r)-1)Delta(G) + epsilon m. F2 is the sum of the squares of the two largest positive adjacency eigenvalues with missing terms padded by zero. The graphs may be disconnected. A companion theorem establishes agreement with the two largest ordered eigenvalue squares in the same eventual range. Enough edges force an F-free graph to be noncomplete; BN nonedge interlacing gives a nonnegative second ordered eigenvalue, so its positive-two energy equals the first two ordered eigenvalue squares. The proof checks ordinary clique removal through regularity and clique counting, derives weighted deletion, reuses the proved BN rank-two Gram inequality, and supplies the spectral lift, hub separation and uniform assembly.
